# DSH Studio v0.7.5

This patch release focuses on macOS first-run compatibility and cross-platform
startup stability. It fixes Homebrew Node installations being rejected as if
npm were absent, closes a managed-runtime/profile fallback race, and adds a safe
route to the DSH Hub community directory.

## Added

- The plugin Sources view now opens DSH Hub for community discovery.
- The UI explains the boundary: bring an npm package name back to Studio, where
  exact version, integrity, repository backlink, Harness peer range and
  lifecycle-script checks still apply.

## Changed and secured

- Harness setup selects the newest compatible Node that has working npm;
  Harness startup may still use the newest compatible Node overall.
- Studio validates an npm entry by running `npm-cli.js --version` with the exact
  selected Node, never a same-named shim found elsewhere on PATH.
- Existing profiles retain the pnpm store recorded by pnpm itself. New profiles
  use a stable Studio-owned store, reducing failures after global pnpm
  configuration changes.
- DSH Hub is currently a website directory, not a Studio Schema 1.0.0 API.
  Studio opens it externally, does not scrape its HTML or execute web-provided
  commands, and keeps its native install policy intact.
- The desktop bridge remains Protocol 3. Harness stays pinned to
  `@deepseek-ai/dsh@0.1.0-rc.8` and pnpm to 11.7.0.

## Fixed and polished

- Fixed [#3](https://github.com/Moresyl/dsh-studio/issues/3): after Homebrew's
  `node` symlink resolves into `/opt/homebrew/Cellar/...` or
  `/usr/local/Cellar/...`, Studio now recognizes both formula `libexec` and
  prefix-shared npm layouts on Apple Silicon and Intel Macs.
- When a compatible user Node truly has no working npm, online setup downloads
  official Node, verifies the publisher SHA-256, installs it under Studio app
  data and resumes the original Harness installation automatically.
- Fixed Environment checks, tray/window startup and Repair racing while the
  managed Harness runtime and profile module fallback were being refreshed.
  These operations now share one lifecycle gate and wait for supervised
  shutdown before runtime promotion.
- Initial retry is restricted to a managed `@deepseek-ai/*` module temporarily
  missing from a profile. Third-party plugin, configuration and unrelated module
  failures still fail immediately with their diagnostics intact.
- Fixed manual Actions releases treating the branch name `main` as the Release
  tag while uploading the Windows portable build. Manual and tag releases now
  resolve the configured version consistently.

## Install and update

Homebrew Node users and anyone who saw intermittent profile-module or
`harness closed its output without announcing a port` failures should upgrade.
Existing profiles, plugins, workspaces and sessions are preserved, and existing
pnpm stores are not forcibly migrated.

Verify downloads with `SHA256SUMS.txt`; in-app updates still require the Tauri
updater signature. Windows Authenticode and Apple Developer ID are separate OS
publisher signatures and depend on external credentials configured for the
release repository.
